name: kimi-git-flow
description: Kimi Code plugin that turns every code change into a clean, reviewable update on GitHub.
skillInstructions: When the user asks for a code change in a git repo, follow the kimi-git-flow procedure (full reference at skills/git-flow/SKILL.md): create a fresh branch named after the repository's branch-naming convention, from the detected default branch, commit the change on it, run the local check (step 2.5) against the working tree, push and open a pull request with `gh pr create`, wait for required checks with `gh pr checks --watch`, then land the change with `gh pr merge --squash` once green (the remote branch is kept by default; pass `--delete-branch` only when `KIMI_GIT_FLOW_DELETE_REMOTE_BRANCH=1`), and switch the working copy back to the default branch. Hard rules: never force-push the default branch, never pass --admin to gh pr merge, never merge with red CI, never co-mingle unrelated changes, never run `git checkout --` / `git reset --hard` / `git stash drop` / `git clean -fd` mid-workflow without explicit user approval (silent revert), never start a new branch while the local default branch has unpushed commits — push, rebase, or drop them first.

interface.shortDescription: Branch → pull request → wait for checks → land, one branch per change.
interface.longDescription: Kimi Code plugin that turns every code change into a clean, reviewable update on GitHub. Creates an isolated branch, runs a local check against the working tree, opens a pull request, waits for the required checks, and lands the change automatically. Exposes slash commands (/branch, /pr, /watch, /merge, /status, /back-to-main, /setup-ci) for fine-grained control. /setup-ci is opt-in and scaffolds a minimal GitHub Actions workflow when the repo has none. GitHub-only; uses `gh` and `git` directly.
